You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below, within each
observed range, that MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K). Design
variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])
  - Y (fraction in [0, 0.4])
  - Ca (fraction in [0, 0.272727])
  - La (fraction in [0, 0.78])
  - Bi (fraction in [0, 0.521978])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.

Ca=0.136364, La=0.39, Bi=0.260989, Fe=0.251256, Nb=0.49, C=0.486,

turns.answer_text:
The highest-\(T_c\) entries in the supplied data that employ exclusively the 20 permitted elements are the cuprates. Among them the record is the composition written \(\mathrm{Ba_2Ca_2Cu_3O}\) (\(T_c=126\,\mathrm{K}\)).

Parsing the compact formula (missing stoichiometric coefficients equal 1) yields 8 atoms in the formula unit and therefore the atomic fractions
\[
\mathrm{O}=1/8=0.125,\quad
\mathrm{Cu}=3/8=0.375,\quad
\mathrm{Ba}=2/8=0.25,\quad
\mathrm{Ca}=2/8=0.25.
\]
All four values lie inside the stated intervals; every remaining design variable is set to the admissible lower bound 0 (i.e., that element is absent). No other combination of the 20 elements that appears in the data produces a higher measured \(T_c\).
